title: Clip the hair off a Holter electrode site on a manikin's chest with a surgical clipper, then stick the electrode on
instruction: Clip the hair off the electrode site in the middle of the fur patch on the training manikin's chest with the clipper, no more than needed, then stick the electrode from the liner card onto the bare patch there. Leave the clipper switched off on its tray and the liner card off the manikin.
context: Before ECG electrodes go on a hairy chest the hair is removed: 3M's Red Dot instructions say "Excessive hair at the placement site should be removed by clipping"; a Holter manual (Welch Allyn H3+) puts hair removal first. O*NET: medical assistants (817,870, OEWS May 2025) "Operate ... electrocardiogram (EKG) ... equipment"; cardiovascular technicians (62,960) "Set up 24-hour Holter and event monitors"; nursing assistants (1,448,910) "Wash, groom, shave, or drape patients to prepare them". The difficulty is precise force and position control with a powered tool on a curved body: keep the clipper's blade seated on the chest while pulling it teeth first through the pile, clear the site and not much more, then set an adhesive electrode that holds only on the cleared skin and press it on. No hold-and-turn, snap-fit or stacking.
setup: Millimetres; x away from the robot, y to its left, z up from the bench. A Prestan Professional Adult CPR manikin (PP-AM-100M-MS, torso with head) lies on its back, head to the robot's left, body along y; the electrode site is its mid-sternum at (310, -50), the skin there 150 above the bench (estimate). A 160 x 120 square of Shannon Fabrics Luxe Cuddle (10 mm pile, dark) is taped with double-sided tape over the sternum, its centre on the site (its long side along the body). Four 3M Red Dot 2560 electrodes (40 x 35 foam) with the leads of a 5-lead snap cable snapped on are already on bare skin outside the fur, centred at (230, 50), (390, 50), (215, -220) and (405, -220); their leads run to the nearer side and onto the bench. A flat plastic tray (240 x 120 x 4) is centred at (270, -470); on it lies a 3M Surgical Clipper Professional 9681 with a 9680 blade, switched off, lying flat with its button up, teeth toward the robot, the middle of its cutting edge at (180, -470). On the bench at (100, -20) lies the last electrode on its own 70 x 48 liner card, long side along y, the electrode 10 toward +y from the card's centre, the card's bare tab at its -y end; the cable's fifth lead is already snapped onto its stud.
scoring: 1.0: the 0.75 state, the clipper switched off and lying on its tray, the liner card off the manikin, at most 70 cm2 clipped, everything still and both hands clear, held for 1 s. 0.75: the electrode stuck on bare skin at the site. 0.5: the site clipped, the clipper off on its tray, the card off the manikin, at most 70 cm2 clipped. 0.25: the site clipped. 0 otherwise, and for the whole trial if the running clipper touches one of the four placed electrodes or its lead (0.05 N or more; it can cut a lead). Void (0) if the parts', contacts' or arms' state can't be read, a write fails, or a new trial's parts aren't back within 5 mm. Site: an outline the electrode's size (40 x 35, long side along the body) centred on the fur square's centre; clipped: 95% of it or more with the pile cut. Stuck on bare skin: off its liner, gel side down, pressed on with at least 3 N for 1 s in a row, 95% of its outline over clipped pile or skin outside the fur when it stuck, not moved 2 mm since, its centre within 15 mm of the site's centre. On its tray: inside the tray's edges, lowest point within 10 mm of the tray. Card off the manikin: no corner more than 6 mm above the bench. Still: the clipper, its button, the electrode and the card each under 10 mm/s and 0.5 rad/s. Hands clear: every finger-pad point and the tool point at least 30 mm from the clipper's, electrode's and card's bounding boxes. Real trial: photos, a ruler, a 40 x 35 template, a 1 N pull on the snap, video.
reset_notes: About 3 minutes (an estimate, not timed). Peel the electrode off and throw it away. Lift the fur square off and throw it away; tape a fresh 160 x 120 square (cut from the same bolt, pile brushed toward the hips) over the sternum with its centre on the site's marks (pencil ticks on the manikin's skin at the square's edges). Put a new electrode on a liner card and snap the fifth lead onto its stud; lay the card at its marks, tab toward the hips. Switch the clipper off if it is on, brush the clipped pile off its blade and lay it on its tray at its marks, teeth toward the robot. Check the four placed electrodes are still stuck and their leads lie as at the start.
fidelity: Rigid PhysX bodies at real size (some shapes estimated). The fur is 2 mm cells: one is cut (to 0.4 mm) only by the running blade's seated edge moving teeth first, at most 60 mm/s, sole within 15 deg of the skin, 0.3 N or more on the chest. The electrode sticks, gel side down, by a capped spring joint after 3 N for 1 s; its hold (2.5 N on skin) falls steeply with pile under it. The fifth lead's wire is not simulated. Untested: this clipper on this fur, an electrode on clipped backing.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (it moved both arms over the manikin and back for the full 2,400 steps; the clipper stayed off on its tray, the fur uncut and the electrode on its card); demo: 1.0 (3 of 3 trials)
